name: code-comparison
title: Code Comparison
description: A component which compares two code snippets side by side. Dependency-free: plain code gets Shiki-style `[!code highlight|++|--|focus]` notations, and any highlighter (e.g. Shiki) can be plugged in.

examples.name: code-comparison-demo
examples.title: Highlight, diff and focus
examples.description: `// [!code highlight]`, `// [!code ++]`, `// [!code --]` and `// [!code focus]` comments style their line. Hover a side to unblur it.

examples.name: code-comparison-diff
examples.title: Diff
examples.description: Notations work in any comment style: `//`, `#`, `/* */`, `<!-- -->`.

examples.name: code-comparison-highlighter
examples.title: Custom highlighter
examples.description: Pass `highlighter` to colour the code — Shiki's `codeToHtml`, or anything returning the same markup.

props.name: language
props.description: Language of the snippets (e.g. `"typescript"`), passed to `highlighter`.

props.name: filename
props.description: File name shown above both sides.

props.name: highlighter
props.type: (code: string, options: { language, lightTheme, darkTheme }) => string | Promise<string>
props.description: Optional syntax highlighter returning Shiki-shaped HTML (`<pre><code><span class="line">`). Magic UI bundles Shiki; here it's opt-in so the component has no dependencies. With Shiki: `(code, { language, lightTheme, darkTheme }) => codeToHtml(code, { lang: language, themes: { light: lightTheme, dark: darkTheme }, defaultColor: false, transformers: [transformerNotationHighlight(), transformerNotationDiff(), transformerNotationFocus()] })` — dual-theme output follows the page's `dark` class automatically. Define it outside your component (or memoise it): a new function re-highlights. Without a highlighter (or if it throws), the code is shown as plain text with the notations applied.
